title: Employee Scheduling Problem v3.0 - declarative form
description: The problem as a human or the wizard authors it: contracts, employees, demand buckets, and a per-employee-per-day CSV of requirements. What a worker MAY work is implied; transformer/transform.py compiles this into the expanded form, which states it explicitly. Standalone: this file does not reference any other schema. Symbols in square brackets refer to MathematicalDefinition7.

scheduleInput.description: Per-employee-per-day requirements, held as a CSV matrix (one row per employee, one column per date).

dataFile.description: Path to schedule_input.csv, relative to this file.

dayOffCodes.description: Declares and classifies every non-standard cell code, keyed by the code. A custom code can only ever mean the worker is off (work is expressed by A, numbers, and EQUALS/INCLUDE/EXCEPT), so this one map both declares valid codes and says what each means. Each code has exactly one kind, so it cannot be both soft and hard. Both kinds feed the per-week working-day equality n_wk = open days - |unavailable| - |preferable|, so a misclassification shifts that week's target.

kind.description: 'preferable' [D_wk]: soft -- the worker would rather be off, but may be scheduled at a penalty. 'unavailable' [U_wk]: hard -- no assignment permitted. VAC and NOT, if used, must be 'unavailable'.

name.description: Optional short human-readable label for this code.

description.description: Optional longer explanation. Author/UI label only -- the solver ignores it.

FDO.name: Folga obrigatoria
FDO.description: Mandatory day off -- cannot be scheduled

competenceLevel.description: Proficiency in a competency [l_ws]. LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST; larger numbers are progressively lower. A demand.priorityOrder entry naming level 1 therefore means that competency's most senior workers.

timeGrid.description: Cuts the day into the timeslots the model reasons over [T]. Every interval boundary must land on this grid.

slotMinutes.description: Timeslot length. Must divide 1440 (the enum is exactly its divisors). Smaller is more precise but grows the model: 15 gives 96 slots/day, 60 gives 24.

temporalScope.description: The scheduling horizon [D]. start and end are full calendar dates -- the sole source of WHEN the schedule is for (the year lives here, and in every CSV date column). The number of schedule_input date columns must equal this span.

weekStart.description: First day of the week. Defines the week partition [K, D_k] that per-week limits and the working-day count [n_wk] are counted over.

holidays.description: Public holidays. Marking a day here does NOT make anyone unavailable: it exists so the enterprise can give that day its own minimum/empiric/maximum in demand.csv. Shops open on holidays, and whether a worker is entitled to take one off is a per-employee rule (deferred; see FUTURE.md). A holiday reaches a worker's unavailable set [U_wk] only through their schedule-input cell, like any other day.

code.description: Optional short identifier for this holiday (e.g. 'XMAS'). Author/UI label only -- the solver ignores it; the date is the identifier.

description.description: Optional longer explanation. Author/UI label only -- the solver ignores it.

hasEve.description: Whether the preceding day counts as this holiday's eve, so it can carry its own demand. The eve's date is the holiday's date minus one day; only whether it exists needs stating.

workMinutesPerDay.description: Paid minutes per day, used when a schedule-input cell says 'A'. Minutes throughout, so 7h45 is 465.

contractAssignments.description: Which contract applies over which dates. Multiple entries allowed and may be discontinuous (a seasonal worker returning), but must not overlap.

competencyAssignments.description: Which competencies [S_w] the worker holds over which dates, each with a proficiency level. Holding several competencies at once is normal; two entries for the SAME competency must not overlap.

demand.description: Coverage wanted. The per-date numbers live in the CSV named by dataFile; this section carries the structure they reference.

dataFile.description: Path to demand.csv, relative to this file. Columns: date,workPeriod,competency,minimum,empiric,maximum,start,end -- see FORMAT.md.

competencies.description: Competencies. These are the skill dimension [S]; demand is keyed on them and every worker holds them at a level.

code.description: Short identifier used to reference this competency (demand.csv, teamAssignments, priorityOrder).

description.description: Optional longer explanation. Author/UI label only -- the solver ignores it.

workPeriods.description: The buckets demand is keyed on: a demand.csv row names one of these and states how many workers that slice of the day wants. Together they also delimit the operating window. These are NOT a menu of shifts a worker picks from -- asking for one person on an 11:00-21:00 bucket is not asking anyone to work ten hours. What a worker may actually work is a contiguous block of their contracted length, anywhere on the grid inside the operating window.

code.description: Short identifier used to reference this work period (demand.csv workPeriod column).

description.description: Optional longer explanation. Author/UI label only -- the solver ignores it.

timeRange.description: An end at or before the start means the bucket crosses midnight: 22:00-06:30 spans minutes 1320-1830.

priorityOrder.description: Which competency/level combinations to fill first. Ordered and sparse: sort entries by `order` ascending, then the FIRST entry matching a worker's (competency, level) decides their priority. A bare {competency} matches any level of that competency; add `level` to name one exactly. Any combination not listed sorts last, all tied -- listing is opt-in, and nothing is ever excluded from the model. This drives the objective that steers multi-skilled workers toward the combinations you care about [ObjectiveFunction2]: the solver derives the model's numeric weight [p_sl] from the matched entry's position, so no weights are authored here and there is no direction to get backwards.

order.description: Evaluation position; lower is filled first. Must be unique. Ordering follows this field, NOT array position, so entries can be stored or displayed in any arrangement -- grouped by competency, say -- without changing meaning. Gaps are allowed so entries can be inserted later.

level.description: Optional. Omit to match any level of this competency. Remember level 1 is the HIGHEST, so {competency: X, level: 1} means X's most senior, not its juniors.
